# Results — Study 138 (Random-Forest) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py).  One recipe — a Random Forest
trained on standard technical features (lagged returns, RSI, realised vol, momentum, volume
ratio), evaluated with strict walk-forward (train=504 days, step=63 days) and a shuffled-label
control.  Long when model predicts up; flat otherwise; round-trip cost = 5 bps.  As-of
**2026-06-14**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n bars | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| SPY | 2010-01-04 to 2026-06-12 | 4136 | `fed737ecfc62` |

## Walk-forward accuracy — real model vs shuffled-label control

The shuffled-label model is trained on permuted targets within each fold.  If real
accuracy materially exceeds shuffle accuracy, the features carry genuine information.
If they match, any apparent in-sample "edge" is pure overfitting.

| Arm | OOS obs | Accuracy | Acc vs shuffle |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **RF (real labels)** | 3,611 | **53.5%** | **+0.83pp** |
| RF (shuffled labels) | 3,611 | 52.6% | — |

- The delta is **+0.83 percentage points** — almost nothing.  A gap this small is
  consistent with sampling noise and is not evidence of genuine learning.
- Both models predict "up" roughly **75% of the time**, riding SPY's decade-long bull
  trend.  The positive gross return reflects **beta exposure**, not a directional signal
  the forest learned from features.

## Trading results (long when model predicts up; flat otherwise)

| | Gross Sharpe | Gross HAC t | Net Sharpe (5bp) | Net HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **RF walk-forward (real)** | +0.50 | +2.15 | +0.20 | **+0.86** |
| RF shuffled control | +0.58 | +2.34 | +0.19 | +0.76 |
| Buy-and-hold SPY | +0.86 | — | — | — |

**Critical observation:** the shuffled model has a *higher* gross Sharpe (+0.58 vs +0.50)
and a higher gross t-stat (+2.34 vs +2.15).  The real features add no value over random
label assignment.  Both models underperform passive buy-and-hold (Sharpe +0.86), confirming
this is beta harvesting, not alpha.

## Cost sweep

| Round-trip cost (bps) | Mean net (bps/day) | Sharpe | HAC t |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 (gross) | +2.26 | +0.498 | +2.149 |
| 2.0 | +1.72 | +0.379 | +1.631 |
| 5.0 | +0.91 | +0.200 | +0.858 |
| 10.0 | -0.44 | -0.098 | -0.417 |

At 5 bps (a realistic US equity round-trip) the strategy is statistically indistinguishable
from zero (t = +0.86).  The positive gross return disappears under a mild cost assumption.

| Feature | Importance |
|---|--:|
| ret_lag_4 | 0.1583 |
| ret_lag_2 | 0.1290 |
| ret_lag_1 | 0.1225 |

| rsi | 0.0963 |

Features are approximately uniformly distributed — no single feature dominates, and the
in-sample importance pattern does not persist out-of-sample (the shuffle result confirms this).

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.**  OOS accuracy 53.5% vs shuffle 52.6% (delta = +0.83pp); the shuffled
  model's gross t-stat (2.34) **exceeds** the real model (2.15), confirming both are harvesting
  SPY beta, not a learned directional edge.  Net HAC t = +0.86 at 5 bps — indistinguishable
  from zero.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.**  Net Sharpe +0.20 at 5 bps vs B&H +0.86; the strategy invests
  only ~75% of the time, underperforms a passive index fund, and collapses to negative at
  10 bps cost.  No institution could beat SPY this way.
- **Beats shuffle? — No.**  The shuffled-label model matches or outperforms the real model on
  every gross metric.  This is the study's decisive test: the Random Forest learned nothing
  from the features that a shuffled-label version did not also "learn" from noise.
